SUMMARY: A Public Hearing considering a Variance, Site Plan, and Coastal Development
Permit to allow a 300 square foot addition and 130 square foot balcony for an existing four-story,
two-unit residence in the Multiple Residential, Medium Density zone. The Proposed Project is
categorically exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) per State CEQA
Guidelines 15301 (Class 1 – Existing Facilities). The proposed project is not located within the
appealable area of the Coastal Zone.

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S):

  1. Conduct a public hearing;

  2. Find this project exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant
  to Section 15301 under Class 1 (Existing Facilities) of the CEQA Guidelines, because it
  has no potential to have a significant effect on the environment; and

  3. Adopt Resolution No. PC 26-14 approving a Variance, Site Plan, and Coastal
  Development Permit pursuant to PC#2916 (Attachment 1).

AUTHORIZING GUIDELINES: Avalon Municipal Code (AMC) Sections 9-8.401, 9-8.203.a, and
9-8.103.a authorize the Planning Commission to review and take action on applications for a
Variance, Site Plan, and Coastal Development Permit.

Existing Site and Area Context:

The project site is located on a rectangular lot addressed 150 Middle Terrace. The parcel is
situated south of Lower Terrace and north of Upper Terrace. The lot slopes towards the
northwest.

The project site is currently developed with two units as an attached duplex, jointly addressed
150 Middle Terrace. The upper unit consists of a three-bedroom, three and one half bathroom
floor plan. The lower unit is not within the scope of the proposed project. The property was
originally developed in c1927 and currently has Spanish Colonial design details. Many
substantial additions have been made since that time. The property includes one off-street
autoette parking space in an attached garage.

All abutting properties are in the MD zone and Commercial (C) zone and represent a mix of
single and multi-story residential buildings and open space. A vicinity map, showing adjacent
property addresses and zoning, is provided as Attachment 2 of this report.

Entitlement and Permit History:

The following entitlements have been previously granted for the project site:

  •  PC# 2404 – Approval of height variance, lot coverage variance, and setback variances
  for multiple additions. (December 2009)
   PC#2916 – 150 Middle Terrace

  •  PC#2491 – Approval of minor lot line adjustment to modify Middle Terrace Stairs
  easement. (August 2012)

  •  PC#2699 – Approval of a Transient Rental License and Coastal Development Permit for
  the lower unit. (July 2019)

  •  PC#2824 – Approval of setback, height, and floor area variances for addition of 180 roof
  top addition. (December 2022)

There are no active or recent building permits for this property.

PROJECT DESCRIPTION: The applicant, Jackson Durand of Durand Architectural

  •  Add 300 square feet to the 4th floor of the unit for a new observatory. The room does not
  meet the definition of a bedroom as defined in AMC Section 9-3.602.

  •  Add a new 130 square foot deck expansion to the rear of an existing balcony, accessed
  through the dining room of the main (3rd) floor.

No new bedrooms or bathrooms are included in the scope of work. The proposed architectural

DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS:

Issue 1: Setback, Height, and Floor Area Variances
The applicant is requesting multiple variances from the development standards for the MD zone,
as follows:

  •  Allow a floor area of 139% of gross lot area (3,342 sq. ft) where 120% maximum is
  required by code, and 126% has previously been approved by variance (PC#2824,
  December 2022).

  •  Increase the nonconformity of the existing west side setback (4 ft 6 in) with the addition
  of the top (4th) floor of the building, where 10 ft is required by code, and 0 ft has previously
  been approved by variance (PC#2404, December 2009).

  •  Increase the nonconformity of the existing rear setback (~1 ft) with the addition of the new
  deck, where 10 ft is required by code, and 0 ft has been previously allowed by variance
  (PC#2404, December 2009).

  •  Increase the nonconformity of the height of the building (24 ft) with the increase in the
  floor area of the top (4th) floor, where 14 ft is required by code, and 24 ft has been
  previously allowed by variance (PC#2824, December 2022).

Per AMC Chapter 9-8.405, variances from development standards may be permitted by the
Planning Commission where the special circumstances may deprive a property of privileges
enjoyed by other property in the vicinity and under identical zoning classification, the property is
not granted special privileges beyond those available to similar properties, does not permit a use
that is otherwise not allowed, and complies with the Avalon Local Coastal Program.

This historic development pattern of the “Terraces” geographic area consists of shallow, wide
lots, with multi-story residential structures that terrace up the steep hillsides, giving the area its
name. Many buildings have three, four, or more levels, with numerous open decks on the rear
elevations to take advantage of the expansive views of Avalon Bay. Smaller homes were built in
the area during the early establishment of the city, with increasingly large buildings expanded
and/or constructed moving into the mid-20th century.
   PC#2916 – 150 Middle Terrace
  Page 5

The required development standards for the MD zone were last updated in 1989 (Ordinance No.
851). This ordinance, which focused on updates for building height and bulk throughout the city,
provided calculations for building height in relation to setbacks. However, this ordinance did not
change the underlying 10-foot setback requirement from all property lines, which were set as
part of the City’s comprehensive zoning code update approved in 1979 (Ordinance No. 672),
and the maximum height above street level remains the same for properties with a steep slope.
That said, most of the development in the “Terraces” area is nonconforming to MD zone
development standards, and many variances have been granted pre- and post-1989 for building
and deck setbacks.

The requested variances are consistent with approved development of other residential
properties on sloped lots within the immediate vicinity of the project within the “Terraces”
geographic area. A selection of projects approved within the last 15 years is provided below:

  •  115 Upper Terrace (PC#2465, August 2011), (PC#2492, September 2012), and
  (PC#2719, March 2020). Request to reconstruct and expand a residential duplex. Side
  yard setback of 3 feet 6 inches was approved on at least one side.

  •  156 Middle Terrace (PC#2534, February 2014). A side yard setback of 2 inches was
  approved.

  •  333 Wrigley Terrace Road (PC#2521, August 2018) A rear yard setback of 1-foot was
  approved, and the property has existing 0-foot side yard setbacks on at least one side.

  •  108 Middle Terrace Upper (PC#2912, March 2026) A side setback of 4 ft 9 in and 0 ft
  rear setback variance were approved.

The subject property is currently legally nonconforming for height, setbacks, and floor area due
to the granting of past variances from these development standards, as described above. The
proposed project will increase the floor area of the building, and increase the nonconformity of
setbacks and height, though the construction would be within the limits previously approved via
variance.

According to the permitting records for these projects, the findings for approval for these
variances took into consideration the location and surrounding of adjacent residential
development, including whether the placement of the building on the lot would create nuisance,
privacy, or viewshed issues for adjacent neighbors and allowing the maximum development
potential intended in the zone equal to other existing developed properties in the same area.

Approval of the proposed project can be similarly justified as previous variances. The placement
of the existing building on the property follows the contour of the hillside, with interior and exterior
living areas focused out towards the rear of the property and views of Avalon Bay. The proposed
addition to the deck is parallel with the corresponding deck on the east adjacent property (166
Middle Terrace) and does impose on any of the existing private indoor areas of the home.
Similarly, the rooftop observatory addition (west adjacent to 156 Middle Terrace) does not
introduce any new window or door openings that impact the private living area of that residence,
as the addition is story taller and windows only look down on the roof below. Therefore, the
design of the proposed additions should not create any new nuisance or privacy issues for
adjacent properties.
   PC#2916 – 150 Middle Terrace
  Page 6

Furthermore, while private viewsheds are not explicitly protected by the municipal code, the
building is not proposed to be taller than the existing condition, which will protect existing privacy
and views for adjacent properties on Middle Terrace, Upper Terrace, and from nearby public
access viewpoints along Wrigley Terrace Road.

Therefore, it is the opinion of staff that the proposed variances may be granted in conformance
with the findings of the municipal code, as there are special circumstances related to location
and surroundings that would otherwise deprive the property of the development potential of other
flat lots within the same zone, the variances do not constitute granting of special privileges and
similar variances have previously been granted for the same use on similarly sloped lots within
the same zone and geographic area of the city, and the building fits within the context of the
existing development and topography in the surrounding area.

GENERAL PLAN, LAND USE, AND ZONING COMPLIANCE:

Pursuant AMC Sections 9-8.405, 9-8.203, and 9-8.103.d, recommended findings for approval of
a Variance, Site Plan, and Coastal Development Permit are provided in draft Resolution No. PC
26-14 (Attachment 1).

Annual Growth Policy

The growth policy provides that new residential or commercial development should only be
permitted with confirmation from Southern California Edison Company (“SCE”) that adequate
fresh water is available. Water demand for residential buildings is calculated based on the
number of bedrooms in the unit. The project involves internal remodeling and additions to an
existing duplex residential unit, with no increase in bedroom count. Therefore, no additional
water allocation is required to permit the construction of the proposed project. Therefore, staff
recommends that the Planning Commission make the finding that the proposed project is in
compliance with the 2026 Annual Growth Policy.

ENVIRONMENTAL DETERMINATION: The proposed project is categorically exempt from the
provisions of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) per State CEQA Guidelines
15301 (Class 1 – Existing Facilities) because it has no potential to have a significant effect on the
environment.

The Class 1 exemption includes the operation, repair, maintenance, permitting, leasing,
licensing, or minor alteration of existing public or private structures, facilities, mechanical
equipment, or topographical features, involving negligible or no expansion of use. The project
involves permitting of additions to one unit in an existing residential duplex, with no change of
the residential use on the project site, in compliance with applicable development standards and
variance findings. As such, the project is not expected to have a significant environmental impact
on the surrounding area.

Furthermore, the project was evaluated pursuant to the criteria for the exceptions to the
exemptions as identified in Guidelines Section 14 CCR, Chapter 3, Article 19, Section 15300.2
and the Planning Commission finds that there are no exceptions to the use of an exemption for
the project. The project does not impact an environmental resource of hazardous or critical
concern, does not result in cumulative impacts, does not have a significant effect on the

  from nearby public access viewpoints along Wrigley Terrace Road.
  Therefore, it is the finding of the Planning Commission that the proposed variances may
  be granted in conformance with the findings of the municipal code, as there are special
  circumstances related to location and surroundings that would otherwise deprive the
  property of the development potential of other flat lots within the same zone, the variances
  do not constitute granting of special privileges and similar variances have previously been
  granted for the same use on similarly sloped lots within the same zone and geographic area
  of the city, and the building fits within the context of the existing development and
  topography in the surrounding area.

2. Any variance granted shall be subject to such conditions as will assure that the
  adjustment thereby authorized shall not constitute a grant of special privileges
  inconsistent with the limitations upon other properties in the vicinity and zone in
  which such property is situated.

  It is the opinion of the Planning Commission that strict application of the setbacks, floor
  area, and height development standards as written in AMC Section 9-5.305 would deprive
  the subject property of the same privileges enjoyed by other properties within the
  “Terraces” hillside area of Avalon, which is predominantly developed with setbacks less
  than required, height more than allowed, and floor area more than allowed by existing code.
  Standard conditions of approval are included in this resolution to ensure the project
  complies with all building and safety regulations for construction of the proposed project.

  Therefore, granting of the requested variances does not constitute granting of special
  privileges as the variance allows development of the property within the parameters
  intended for the MD zone.

  activity which is not otherwise expressly authorized by the zone regulation governing
  the parcel of property.

  Two-family dwelling units (duplexes) are permitted by right within the MD zone. The
  application does not include a request for any use that is not permitted within the zoning
  district.

  4. No variances shall be granted which reduce or adversely affect access to or along the
  shoreline, including physical or visual qualities of access.

  The project site is located over 336 feet from the mean high tide line of Avalon Bay. The site
  is not adjacent to, nor provides direct or indirect public access, visual or physical, the shoreline
  of Avalon Bay, coastal hillsides or bluffs, or other significant viewsheds identified in the
  Avalon Local Coastal Plan.

  5.  The variance shall be consistent with the Local Coastal Program.

  The proposed project implements the following General Plan Policies:

  Policy II-9 of the Land Use Element:

  “Encourage infill of the City Center area and where appropriate, increase the intensity of
  development on vacant and underutilized properties, in lieu of expanded development
  outward into Avalon’s hillsides, natural areas and open space.”

  The project proposes alterations to an existing duplex residential unit. Individually owned
  lots in Avalon comprise less than 1% of the total city acreage. Therefore, it is important to
  maximize the use of land within the city within the development parameters of each zoning
  district, so long as it is consistent with overall community character. The project is designed
  to maximize the density of development on the property in the urbanized center of Avalon
  consistent with the historic development pattern of the neighborhood. Infill construction
  on the existing lot does not contribute to outward expansion into the surrounding natural
  areas or open spaces at the perimeter of the city.

Site Plan Review:

The proposed Project requires approval of a Site Plan per AMC Section 9-8.201. AMC Section 9-
8.203 sets forth the required findings for approval of a Site Plan Review as follows:

  1. Every use, development of land and application of development standards shall take
  place in compliance with all applicable provisions of this title. (AMC Section 9-
  8.203.a)

  Notwithstanding the requested variances for setbacks, height, and floor area, the proposed
  project otherwise complies with all development standards as set forth in AMC for

  6
   development on the project site in the Multiple Residential, Medium Density (MD) zone.
  The project has requested variances for setbacks, height, and floor area pursuant to the
  AMC that are consistent with developments within the “Terraces” hillside area of Avalon,
  as discussed in Variance Findings #1 thought 5.

2. Every use, development of land and application of development standards shall be
  considered on the basis of the suitability of the site for the particular use or
  development intended, and the total development, including the application of
  prescribed development standards, shall be so arranged as to avoid traffic congestion,
  insure the protection of public health, safety and general welfare, prevent adverse
  effects on neighboring property and shall be in general accord with all elements of the
  General Plan. (AMC Section 9-8.203.b)

  The proposed project is designed to fit within the density, scale, and mass of existing
  development along Middle Terrace. This area is locally known as the “Terraces”, a hillside
  residential area, bounded generally by Lower Terrace to the north and Wrigley Terrace
  Road to the south, with dramatically sloping topography and expansive views of Avalon
  Bay. Existing residential development varies in height, with buildings with three or more
  levels common due to the steep slope of the lots. With the additions to the existing deck
  and upper residential unit, the building still fits in with the overall mass and scale of
  surrounding development.

  The project site is located on the north side of Middle Terrace, which is only accessible via
  Wrigley Terrace Road. Wrigley Terrace Road is heavily traveled by both residents and
  visitors accessing scenic viewpoints, such as Buena Vista Point and Mt. Ada, and is
  identified as a Major Circulation Facility in the General Plan Circulation Element. Middle
  Terrace is very narrow due to the slope of the hillside, and is lightly traveled by residents
  and transient rental guests, since it is a dead-end road with no through access. There have
  been no reported traffic issues associated with the residence, and adequate off-street
  parking for both units is provided on the property. Therefore, it is anticipated that existing
  infrastructure will ensure that traffic associated with the residence will not interfere with
  circulation along Middle Terrace.

  The project site is located in an area with access to all necessary utilities and services to
  support the proposed use, including electric, water, gas, sewer, saltwater, and internet.

3. Every use, development of land, application of development standards shall be
  considered on the basis of suitable and functional development design, but is not
  intended that such approval be interpreted to require a particular style or type of
  architecture. (AMC Section 9-8.203.c)

  The project site is located within a developed area of Avalon, on an urbanized parcel
  surrounded by other residential buildings. The design elements in the proposed plans are
  internally consistent with the architecture of the building. The additions are also consistent
  with the established scale of the buildings and structures within the community and will
  not stand out as inconsistent with existing development on the site or in the vicinity.

on the following findings:

  1. The use is in conformance with the certified Local Coastal Program. (AMC 9-
  8.103.d.1)

  Determination of conformance for projects within the City of Avalon includes analysis of
  whether the proposed project conforms with the Avalon General Plan, the Local Coastal
  Plan for Avalon, as well as adopted zoning regulations, as applicable.

  •  General Plan/Local Coastal Plan: The requirements of the Multiple Residential,
  Medium Density (MD) zoning designation of the project site are consistent with the
  General Plan land use designation of Medium Density Residential (MDR).

  The proposed project implements the General Plan Goals and Policies described in
  Variance Finding #5.

  •  California Coastal Act: The proposed project complies with the following sections of
  the Coastal Act:

  Section 30250:

  “(a) New residential, commercial, or industrial development, except as otherwise
  provided in this division, shall be located within, contiguous with, or in close proximity
  to, existing developed areas able to accommodate it or, where such areas are not able
  to accommodate it, in other areas with adequate public services and where it will not
  have significant adverse effects, either individually or cumulatively, on coastal
  resources. In addition, land divisions, other than leases for agricultural uses, outside
  existing developed areas shall be permitted only where 50 percent of the usable parcels
  in the area have been developed and the created parcels would be no smaller than the
  average size of surrounding parcels.”

  The proposed project involves improvements within a developed residential lot in an
  urbanized area of the city, with minimal increase in overall lot coverage and floor area,
  and no change of use of the project site. The project site is located approximately 336
  feet from the nearest coastline (Avalon Bay) and does not contain any coastal resources,
  publicly accessible coastal viewpoint, or coastal access point. Therefore, the area can
  accommodate the proposed project and will not have an individual or cumulative effect
  on coastal resources.

  •  Multiple Residential, Medium Density Development Standards: With approval of the
  proposed variances for side and rear setbacks, the proposed project complies with all

   development standards as set forth in AMC Section 9-5.305 for buildings in the MD
  zone, including lot coverage, floor area, height, and setbacks.

Existing Site and Area Context:

The project site is located on a regularly shaped parcel addressed 228 Catalina Avenue. The
parcel is situated north of Beacon Street and south of Third Street. The lot is relatively flat with
minimal slope, totaling 1,790 square feet.

The project site is located in the Special Commercial zoning district, where residential use
requires a Conditional Use Permit. The existing residence was constructed in 1935, prior to the
requirement of a conditional use requirement. Therefore, the existing residence and residential
use is legally nonconforming. New and modified residential properties within the Special
Commercial zone district are currently required to comply with Multiple-Residential, High Density
(HD) development standards.

The project site is currently developed with a single-story, single-family residence, consisting of
two bedrooms, one bathroom, a kitchen, and living room totaling 989 square feet. The
architecture of the building is a Spanish style, similar to many other residential buildings in “the

right of way, including the rear of Vons. Adjacent to the east is a one-story residential building,
addressed 226 Catalina Avenue. Adjacent to the west is a two-story hotel, Old Turner Inn (232

DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS:

Issue 1: Expansion of Nonconforming Residential Use

Per AMC Chapter 9-6.303, residential structures within the Special Commercial zone district
may be permitted by a conditional use permit, effective February 12, 1986. The existing
residential use was constructed prior to the conditional use requirement for residential structures
in the applicable zone. This creates a legal, non-conformity in the residential structure, permitting
the use without the conditional use permit requirement.

However, AMC Section 9-8.702 Termination of Nonconforming Uses, states that increasing or
enlarging the area, space or volume occupied by a nonconforming use shall terminate the right
to operate the existing nonconforming use.

This issue would be resolved with approval of a CUP for a residential structure, which will make
the use and building conforming to the requirements for the SC zone. The site currently operates
as a single-family residence and is adjacent to single family residences along Catalina Avenue
and Descanso Avenue. There are a variety of commercial uses that also surround the property,
including the Old Turner Inn hotel and Vons grocery shopping. The proposed project fits with the
scale of development and mix of uses in the area and is consistent with the intent for the SC
zone.

Issue 2: Variance for Setbacks and Parking

Per AMC Section 9-8.703.a.4, a nonconforming building or structure located on a lot which is
less than 2,200 square feet may only be altered and maintain its nonconforming status as it
relates to parking, setbacks or height if the alteration or improvement results in an increase of
less than 50% of the square footage of the existing or previously existing structure. Since the
proposed project shall increase the square footage of the building by more than 50%, then the
project must either comply with applicable setbacks and parking or be granted a variance.

Per AMC Section 9-6.303.b, residential structures are subject to the High Density Residential
Building Development Standards. The existing residential building does not conform to existing
code requirements in relation to the required setbacks.

In the designated area of the HD zone, properties that abut an alley are permitted reduced
setbacks as follows:

  “Properties Which Abut an Alley. Except as provided herein, where the property abuts an
  alley, there shall be not less than a three-foot setback on one side and a minimum twelve-
  inch setback on the opposite side. A zero foot sideyard setback may only be allowed on
  the property line if the adjoining property (a) has been developed to the adjoining property
  line and the owner thereof agrees in a recorded document that upon demolition of the
  existing property it shall be reconstructed with the same zero-foot setback or (2) is
  undeveloped and the owner thereof accepts in a recorded document the proposed zero-
  foot setback and further agrees to develop his property to the property line on that side.”

“Opposite sides” is interpreted by staff to mean those properties lines that are opposite of each
other – for a rectangular-shaped lot, this means front and rear setbacks are opposites as well
as opposite/parallel side setbacks. Therefore, the required front and rear setbacks must be a
minimum of 3 ft on one side and 12 inches (1 ft) on the other. The code is clear that 0 ft sideyard
setbacks are only authorized in the presence of one of two different conditions, neither of which
has been reported to staff as having occurred.

As above, the existing residence is presumed to have been constructed with conforming
setbacks when it was built. The rear setback is 2’2” and a front setback is 12”. However, the
addition of the second floor to the building at the same setbacks as the existing building will
increase the nonconformity of the rear setback compared to current code requirements, which
cannot be maintained per the nonconforming structures regulations. Therefore, the rear setback
for the property is 10” too shallow to meet required setbacks for the HD zone without a variance.

The proposed second story addition requires a variance to maintain the existing rear setback of
2’2”. The property is an individually owned property, which compromises less than 1% of the
total city acreage. Therefore, it is important to maximize the use of land within the city within
development parameters of each zoning district, as long as it is consistent with the overall
community character. The surrounding properties along Catalina Avenue and Descanso Avenue
are predominantly developed with reduced setbacks and more than one story. The site was
originally constructed with reduced setbacks prior to setback requirements. The proposed
second-floor addition will be constructed entirely within the existing building footprint. Therefore,
the proposed addition with the continued reduced setback will not negatively impact the
surrounding character and will allow the property to enjoy privileges enjoyed by other properties
in the vicinity.

Parking

Per AMC Section 9-5.405.f, one off-street autoette parking space is required per dwelling unit.
As previously discussed, the property was built prior to adoption of the existing off-street parking
regulations, and no off-street parking space is currently provided. Therefore, the property does
not meet the minimum parking requirements per the municipal code.

The site does not contain an area to provide a parking space without obstruction of access to
the main entrance of the residence and would also require a curb cut on Catalina Avenue. Due
to the location of the existing building on the property, there is no room to add a parking space
accessible from the rear alley behind the residence.

It has been the practice of the Planning Commission and City Council to avoid addition of curb
cuts along street frontages, to avoid the loss of publicly available on-street parking spaces,
especially in parking congested commercial areas of the city. The property is located on the 200-
block of Catalina Avenue, in an area striped for 1-hour parking due to high demand and turnover
of parking in the area.

The subject property contains unique characteristics in the legal, non-conforming residence
constructed in 1935, and if the strict application of the parking requirement was applied, it would
create a physical hardship for the applicant to relocate the existing entrance to the residence.
Other residential properties along the 200-block of Catalina Avenue either have no off-street
parking or access from the alley, with no curb cuts along the main road. Not requiring a curb cut
for off-street parking is consistent with the development pattern on this particular block.
Furthermore, the loss of an on-street parking space along the 200-block of Catalina Avenue
would contribute to additional parking congestion along a busy commercial street, which would
constitute an adverse impact the surrounding properties. Therefore, the findings can be made
for the parking variance.

Existing Site and Area Context:

The project site is located on a rectangular parcel (APN 7480-005-034) addressed 708 Crescent
Avenue, known as the Trailhead Visitor Center. The parcel is situated at the southeast corner of
“the Elbow”, the bend where Crescent Avenue, which generally runs east to west, turns north
and becomes Pebbly Beach Road.

The Trailhead Visitor Center is located at the primary entry point for visitors to the city as they
arrive at the Cabrillo Mole and transit into town. The area is characterized by a mix of visitor-
serving commercial buildings directly on the right-of-way, integrated and adjacent residential
uses, and city parks, including Avalon City Park to the south of the project site. The building itself
is set back from the Elbow and oriented west towards Crescent Avenue.

The Trailhead Visitor Center functions as the hub for the Catalina Island Conservancy visitor
serving functions, including tour sales, retail sales, public permit center, meeting spaces,
Wildland Express shuttle hub, and also acts as the official “Mile 0” of the Trans-Catalina Trail
hiking route. The second floor of the building includes the Topside restaurant, which includes
outdoor dining patios with views of Avalon harbor.

All abutting properties are zoned either Commercial (C) or Resort Recreation (R/R) and
represent a mix vacant commercial, residential, and public open space uses. A vicinity map,
showing adjacent property addresses and zoning, is provided as Attachment 2 of this report.

The graphics will be non-illuminated, and feature imagery and commercial messages relevant
to the services provided at the Trailhead Visitor Center.

According to the applicant, the installation is intended to function as a unified environmental
graphic integrated into the storefront architecture rather than multiple competing signs, reducing
visual clutter while maintaining compatibility with Avalon's pedestrian-oriented visual
environment.

Per AMC Section 9-7.709(j), “[s]igns in the Commercial or Special Commercial zone shall not
exceed an area of eight square feet per face.” As such, the applicant has requested a sign

DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS:

Issue 1: Sign Variance Findings

AMC Section 9-7.728 sets forth specific sign variance findings that are similar to, but separate
from, the standard variance findings in the municipal code. In summary, a sign variance may be
granted only after proof to the Planning Commission that the variance does not constitute a grant
of special privilege, is not inconsistent with the use of surrounding properties in the immediate
location, is granted only to overcome practical difficulties to prevent unnecessary hardship, and
will not result in material damage or be detrimental to the public safety and welfare.

It is the opinion of staff that the requested sign variance meets the intent of the required findings
for approval. The granting of the sign variance will also not constitute granting of a special
privilege and is consistent with similar sign variances granted for other properties in the
immediate vicinity, including 104 Clarissa Avenue (PC#2766, October 2021), 513 Crescent
Avenue (Pavilion Hotel) (No PC#, April 2010), and the subject property itself (PC#2649,
February 2018). These approvals were based on allowing additional signage that is compatible
with the pedestrian scale of the commercial zone and enhance wayfinding for pedestrians to
locate local businesses when their location or architecture may make them less visible to the
public.

The project site is located on a primary commercial corridor and the applicant is advertising
commercial services consistent with surrounding uses. The main entrance to the Trailhead
Visitor Center, where the signage is proposed, is set back from Crescent Avenue due to the
configuration of the “Elbow”. This reduces visibility of the storefront compared to other
commercial buildings in the immediate vicinity. Allowing the window graphics to be installed will
provide additional visibility for visitors who access the services at the visitor center.

Furthermore, the proposed signage will not cause adverse impacts to surrounding uses or create
safety issues. As previously stated, the front façade of the building is set back from Crescent
Avenue. Installation of window graphics on the existing storefront will not create any visibility
issues for pedestrians or vehicles passing through the area, nor will it block view of the signage
for any surrounding businesses. Installation does also not require any material change to
surrounding public or private property, as the graphics will be installed on the existing building
storefront.

Therefore, staff recommends that findings for approval of the project can be made for both the
sign variance findings, and to allow a categorical exemption from CEQA, as outlined in the draft
resolution included as Attachment 1.

filed an application (“Application”) for a Sign Variance (PC#2919) to allow vinyl signage on the
façade windows of the Trailhead Visitor Center that is larger than eight (8) square feet (“Project”)
on the property located at 708 Crescent Avenue, APN 7480-005-034 (“Site”); and

  WHEREAS, Avalon Municipal Code (AMC) Section 9-7.709(j) states in part that “[s]igns
in the Commercial or Special Commercial zone shall not exceed an area of eight square feet per
face”; and

  WHEREAS, the Project proposes installing non-illuminated perforated vinyl window
graphics at the Site, featuring scenic Catalina landscapes, interpretive map imagery, recreation
themes, and visitor information associated with services available at the Trailhead Visitor Center;
and

  WHEREAS, the entire windowed portion of the façade of the Site is approximately two
hundred nineteen (219) square feet;

  WHEREAS, the Project is anticipated to cover all the sealed windows on the façade of the
Site, an area estimated to be approximately one hundred ninety (190) square feet;

  WHEREAS, the front doors of the Site make up the remaining approximately twenty-nine
(29) square feet of windowed area on the façade; however, the Project is anticipated to only cover
a portion of this area;

  WHEREAS, the Planning Commission has authority per AMC Section 9-7.727 to review
and take action on the subject application for a Sign Variance, pursuant to the requirements in
AMC Section 9-7.728; and

  WHEREAS, the Site is categorized Commercial by the General Plan Land Use Element
and is located within the designated area of the Commercial (C) zoning district; and

  WHEREAS, the Site is located within the Coastal Zone and is within the planning
boundaries of the Avalon Local Coastal Program; and

  WHEREAS, the Project was found to be categorically exempt from CEQA per State
CEQA Guidelines 15301 (Class 1 – Existing Facilities). No public review is required; and

based on the following findings:

SECTION 1 – INCORPORATION OF RECITALS
The Planning Commission hereby finds that the foregoing recitals are true and correct and are
incorporated herein as substantive findings.

SECTION 2 – ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW
The proposed project is categorically exempt from the provisions of the California Environmental
Quality Act (CEQA) per State CEQA Guidelines 15301 (Class 3 – Existing Facilities) because it
has no potential to have a significant effect on the environment.

The Class 1 exemption includes the operation, repair, maintenance, permitting, leasing, licensing,
or minor alteration of existing public or private structures, facilities, mechanical equipment, or
topographical features, involving negligible or no expansion of use. The project involves
permitting of window signage on an existing commercia building, in compliance with applicable
sign variance findings for signage larger than permitted by code. As such, the project is not
expected to have a significant environmental impact on the surrounding area.

The project was evaluated pursuant to the criteria for the exceptions to the exemptions as identified
in Guidelines Section 14 CCR, Chapter 3, Article 19, Section 15300.2 and the Planning
Commission finds that there are no exceptions to the use of an exemption for the project. The
project does not impact an environmental resource of hazardous or critical concern, does not result
in cumulative impacts, does not have a significant effect on the environment due to unusual
circumstances, does not damage scenic resources within a state scenic highway, does not impact a
historic resource, and is not a hazardous waste site.

SECTION 3 – FINDINGS

Annual Growth Policy:

The growth policy provides that new residential or commercial development should only be
permitted with confirmation from Southern California Edison Company (“SCE”) that adequate
fresh water is available. The proposed project does not include any development that would be
subject to review for additional water service, as it does not include additions or expansion of the
existing commercial use. Therefore, the Planning Commission makes the finding that the proposed
project is in compliance with the 2026 Annual Growth Policy.

  2
 Affordable Housing Ordinance:

AMC Chapter 9-11, Affordable Housing, sets forth inclusionary and employee housing
requirements for new residential and commercial developments within the City. The project
requests a Sign Variance for an existing commercial building, with no new or expanded
commercial development. Therefore, the project is not subject to review for compliance with the
City’s affordable housing regulations.

Sign Variance:

AMC Section 9-7.728 sets forth the required findings for approval of a Sign Variance as follows:

1. A Sign Variance shall not constitute a grant of special privilege and shall be consistent
  with the use of surrounding properties in the immediate location and shall be granted
  only to overcome practical difficulties and to prevent unnecessary hardship in the
  application.

  The requested sign variance meets the intent of the required findings for approval. The granting
  of the sign variance will not constitute granting of a special privilege and is consistent with
  similar sign variances granted for other properties in the immediate vicinity, including 104
  Clarissa Avenue (PC#2766, October 2021), 513 Crescent Avenue (No PC#, April 2010), and
  the subject property itself (PC#2649, February 2018). These approvals were based on allowing
  additional signage that is compatible with the pedestrian scale of the commercial zone and
  enhance wayfinding for pedestrians to locate local businesses when their location or
  architecture may make them less visible to the public.

  The project site is located on a primary commercial corridor and the applicant is advertising
  commercial services consistent with surrounding uses. The main entrance to the Trailhead
  Visitor Center, where the signage is proposed, is set back from Crescent Avenue due to the
  configuration of the “Elbow”. This reduces visibility of the storefront compared to other
  commercial buildings in the immediate vicinity. Allowing the window graphics to be installed
  will provide additional visibility for visitors who access the services at the visitor center.

2. A Sign Variance shall not result in material damage or be detrimental to the public safety
  and welfare.

  The proposed signage will not cause adverse impacts to surrounding uses or create safety
  issues. As previously stated, the front façade of the building is set back from Crescent Avenue.
  Installation of window graphics on the existing storefront will not create any visibility issues
  for pedestrians or vehicles passing through the area, nor will it block view of the signage for
  any surrounding businesses. Installation does also not require any material change to
  surrounding public or private property, as the graphics will be installed on the existing building
  storefront.

  3
 Coastal Development Permit:

The proposed project is located within the Coastal Zone and is excluded from Coastal
Development Permit requirements per Avalon Municipal Code (AMC) Section 9-8.102.b.2.
Improvements to an existing structures other than single-family residences or public works
facilities are excluded from CDP review, except those classes of development which involve a risk
of adverse environmental effect, defined as:

  •  Improvements to any structure on a beach, stream or seaward of the mean high tide line.
  •  Any significant alteration of land forms, including removal or placement of vegetation, on
  a beach or within 100 feet of the edge of a coastal bluff or stream;
  •  The expansion or construction of water wells or septic systems;
  •  On property located between the sea and the first public road paralleling the sea or within
  300 feet of the inland extent of any beach, whichever is the greater distance, an
  improvement that would result in:
  o An increase in 10% or more of external floor area of the existing structure, or
  o An additional improvement of 10% or less where an improvement to the structure
  has been previously undertaken pursuant to § 9-8.102A, above.
  o The construction of an additional story (including lofts) in an existing structure.
  •  Any improvement to a structure which changes the intensity of use of the structure;
  •  Any improvement made pursuant to a conversion of an existing structure from a multiple
  unit rental use or visitor-serving commercial use to a use involving a fee ownership or long-
  term leasehold including, but not limited to, a condominium conversion, stock cooperative
  conversion, or motel/hotel time sharing conversion.

The proposed project meets none of the above criteria, therefore it is excluded from the Coastal
Development Permit review process.
